result.title: Target Recoverability under Selective Labels: A Failure Mode in ECG-Based Acute Coronary Syndrome Prediction
result.comment: Accepted to the Proceedings of Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026
result.summary: Medical machine learning models often learn from diagnoses observed only in patients clinicians chose to test. The biases of such selective labels are well known, but less understood is what happens when a diagnosis includes cases the model's inputs cannot detect. Because testing decisions draw on information the model does not see, these cases can appear predictable among tested patients, producing relationships that fail, and can even reverse, among the untested. We formalize this mechanism and show in simulations that it worsens as testing becomes more selective or undetectable cases more common, while models trained only on detectable cases remain informative. We empirically study electrocardiogram (ECG)-based prediction of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), which is confirmed only by invasive testing and whose subtypes differ in how clearly they appear on the ECG. Three ECG foundation models fine-tuned on revascularization, our ACS proxy, performed well among catheterized patients (AUROC 0.740-0.770) but worse than chance for 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events among untested patients (AUROC 0.381-0.478). Models trained on ECG-visible subtypes retained discrimination (AUROC 0.680-0.709), whereas a model trained on unstable angina, which can occur without ECG changes, was inversely related to risk (AUROC 0.310). Under selective labels, effective learning therefore requires prediction targets that can be inferred from the model's inputs and evaluation in the intended deployment population, which often extends beyond the patients who were tested.

AI.brief_summary: 论文形式化“选择性标签”下目标可恢复性失效机制：当标签只在被选择检测的人群中可见、且部分病例无法由模型输入识别时，学到的关系会在未检测人群中失效甚至反转，并以 ECG 预测急性冠脉综合征做实证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“目标能否由输入推断”与在部署人群而非已测人群中评估的形式化，可能为 LVR 中判断答案是否真正依赖视觉 latent、以及筛选可被内部状态支持的预测目标提供概念类比，可供核查。
